g.text: Response — travels opposite to the request path

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
# Demonstrator for `flow left` (maintainer review): direction is # a property of the FIGURE, and a response path is the natural subject for it # — the request went rightward off-stage, and this figure shows the reply # travelling back, so the flow axis runs right to left and the drawing reads # the way the sentence does. One `flow` line per document; a second is a line # error. figdown 0.1 block title "Response path — the reply travels right to left"
class reply "Response — travels opposite to the request path" stroke=#2563eb
node origin "Origin server" node cache "Edge cache" node client "Client"
flow left
edge origin -[200 OK]-> cache class=reply edge cache -[200 OK (cached copy)]-> client class=reply
# Layout zone — and the corpus's negative-coordinate demonstrator, moved here # from the RPF figure when that one went fully automatic. `at=` # is canvas px and the origin is a reference point, not a wall: the parser # accepts a negative component and the layout honours it. Here it lifts the # cache above the reply line, the way a side cache is drawn. # # WHAT A NEGATIVE COORDINATE DOES NOT DO — verified by rendering: it does not # move the page. The canvas grows RIGHT and DOWN only, so a negative # coordinate spends the margin that already exists above the content and # nothing more; past that the element is CLIPPED, not merely misplaced (the # layout gate's offcv axis reports exactly that). A negative x has no margin # to spend at all and always clips. layout pin cache at=(210,-16)
